intro: Professionals and everyday users convert metric horsepower (PS) to horsepower (hp) (hp) when working across metric and imperial standards in automotive engine output ratings, electric motor sizing, solar inverter specifications, and appliance load planning. One horsepower (metric ps) equals 0.98632 horsepower (hp), while 1 horsepower (mechanical) equals 1.01387 metric horsepower. Whether you are verifying power specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Exact NIST Factor vs. Early Rounding Drift
items: The exact conversion factor from Horsepower (Metric PS) to Horsepower (Mechanical) is 0.98632007, derived from the 1959 International Yard and Pound Agreement (1 inch = 25.4 mm, 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg).

In structural engineering, CNC machining, or bulk inventory totals, rounding the multiplier to 2 decimal places too early can introduce cumulative tolerance errors; always compute with the full factor and round only the final displayed figure.

faqs.question: How many horsepower (hp) (hp) are in 1 horsepower (metric ps) (PS)?
faqs.answer: There are 0.98632007 horsepower (hp) (hp) in 1 horsepower (metric ps) (PS), which rounds to 0.9863 hp for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 horsepower (mechanical) equals 1.01387 metric horsepower.

faqs.question: How do I convert metric horsepower to horsepower (hp) (PS to hp)?
faqs.answer: To convert metric horsepower to horsepower (hp), use the formula: hp = PS × 0.98632007. For example, converting 10 PS gives 9.8632 hp.

faqs.question: What is 10 metric horsepower in horsepower (hp)?
faqs.answer: 10 metric horsepower (PS) equals exactly 9.8632 horsepower (hp) (hp) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
